DEEPAK GUPTA, J.
All the present 5 appeals arise out of a common award dated 11.11.2002 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Faridabad, whereby five claim petitions, petitions, all instituted under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, arising out of the same motor vehicular accident accident,, were decided together.

2. As the perusal of record reveal, on 11.10.1997,, Anuraj Kalia, along with Sarita Kalia, Geeta Kalia,
Vikas Kalia, Kalia a six--month-old child Aakrati Kalia,, and Vikas Prabhakar, was travelling from Delhi to Ambala in car bearing registration No. DL-9C-1796 1796,, which was being driven by Anuraj Kalia himself.
When the car reached near Girbari, District Kurukshetra, Kurukshetra, it came to a halt due to a traffic jam.
A truck bearing registration No. HR-03-6197was was standing stationary ahead of the car.

At that moment, a bus bearing registration No. No.DL-1P-3703,, driven by respondent No.1 Satinder Singh, came from the Delhi side at a high speed aand nd in a rash and negligent manner, and rammed into the car from behind.
As a result of the impact, the car was pushed forward and went underneath the stationary truck.

Due to the injuries sustained in the accident:
 Vikas Prabhakar and Aakrati Kalia (aged ssix months) succumbed to their injuries.

The remaining occupants, namely Anuraj Kalia, Sarita Kalia, Geeta Kalia and Vikas Kalia, Kalia, sustained multiple injuries and were initially taken to Nilokheri Hospital and thereafter referred to Karnal for further treatm treatment.

Five claim petitions were filed seeking compensation - one by Anuraj Kalia & Geeta Kalia, Kalia, parents of deceased child Aakrati Kalia; and four by the injured claimants.
There is nothing on record to indicate whether the legal representatives of deceased decea Vikas Prabhakar filed any claim petition.

4. The driver, owner and insurer of the offending bus were impleaded as respondents No.1 to 3, 3, whereas the driver, owner and insurer of the truck were impleaded as respondents No.4 to 6.
5.

Vide the common award award dated 11.11.2002, the learned Tribunal held that the accident occurred due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the bus; and that there was no negligence attributable to the stationary truck.
truck Different amounts of compensation were awarded to the cclaimant.
laimant.
Consequently, respondents No.1 to 3 were held jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation along with interest.

6. All the present appeals have been filed only on the question of quantum of compensation,
compensation, and not on the issue of negligence or liability.
FAO No. 2126 of 2003 (Death of child Aakrati Kalia)
7. The deceased child was six months old at the time of accident.

The learned Tribunal has awarded 50,000/- under no no-fault liability, and 10,000/-
10,000/ towards shock and mental agony, making a total of 60,000/-.
8. Learned counsel for the appellants contends that the compensation awarded is wholly inadequate.

Reliance has been placed upon judicial judicia precedents, where even in the case of children below one year, notional income has been assessed, assessed, keeping in view the future prospects and the principles laid down under the Second Schedule to the Act.

Anurag Kalia vs Satinder Singh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58309153/
3 9.

Though it is not possible to assess the actual iincome ncome of a child of six months, the Supreme Court has consistently held that just compensation cannot be illusory,, and notional income must be adopted to avoid arbitrary figures.
The Second Schedule to Section 163-A 163 A of the Motor Vehicle Act, though not str strictly ictly applicable, can safely be used as a guideline.
Page N: 3 of 6 3 of 6 FAO No. 2126 of 2003 & other connected cases 10.

As such, considering the age of the child, the accident having occurred in the year 1997,, and judicial precedents governing assessment of compensation for minors, this Court deems it appropriate to assess the notional income at 15,000/-
15,000/ per annum,, and by applying the multiplier of 15,, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency works out to 2,25,000/-..
11.
In addition to above, the appellants are entitled to 5,000/- towards funeral expenses, nses, and 10,000/- each towards loss of filial consortium consortium.
12. Thus, the total just compensation comes to 2,50,000/-..

After deducting 60,000/-
60,000/ already awarded by the Tribunal, the appellants are held entitled to enhanced compensation of 1,90,000/ 1,90,000/-.
FAO O No. 2127 of 2003 (Injury to Anuraj Kalia)
13. The appellant sustained simple injuries on the forehead, chest and other parts of the body.
He was not hospitalized and produced no medical bills, though he claimed to have spent 10,000/- on treatment.

The Tribunal awarded a lump sum of 3,000/-.

14.
Even though the injuries were simple, the appellant must have suffered pain, inconvenience and mental trauma.
Compensation must not be merely token.

Accordingly, total compensation is reassessed at 10,000/ 10,000/-, entitling ntitling the appellant to an enhancement of 7,000/
7,000/-.

FAO No. 2128 of 2003 (Injury to Sarita Kalia)
15.
The appellant remained hospitalized from 11.10.1997 to 16.10.1997..
Medical bills amounting to 32,576/ 32,576/- were proved.

The Tribunal awarded only 1,000/-
1,000/ towards pain and suffering, which is grossly inadequate.

16. Considering the duration of hospitalization and the physical suffering undergone, the appellant is held entitled to 30,000/- as lump sum towards pain, suffering, attendant charges and incident Anurag Kalia vs Satinder Singh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58309153/
4 incidental expenses, over and above the amount already awarded.

Page N: 4 of 6 4 of 6 FAO No. 2126 of 2003 & other connected cases FAO No. 2129 of 2003 (Injury to Vikas Kalia)
17.
The appellant remained hospitalized for six days and proved medical expenses of 17,920/-.
Only 1,000/ 1,000/- was awarded for pain and suffering.
18. Applying the same reasoning as in FAO No.2128 of 2003, the Applying appellant is held entitled to an additional 30,000/ 30,000/- as just compensation for pain, suffering and related expenses.
FAO No. 2130 of 2003 (Injury to Geeta Kalia)

19. The appellant remained hospitalized from 11.10.1997 to 29.10.1997,, i.e. for 19 days,, and incurred medical expenses of 60,834/-.
20.
Though no permanent disability was proved, her long hospitalization and uncontroverted testimony that she remained bedridd bedridden en for about six months cannot be ignored.
21. The Tribunal awarded only 2,000/ 2,000/- towards pain and suffering and 5,000/- towards loss of income, which is disproportionately low.
22. Having regard to the nature of injuries, duration of treatment and prolonged onged recovery, the appellant is held entitled to additional compensation of 1,50,000/- in lump sum.
Final Order 22.
Consequently, all five appeals are allowed to the extent indicated below:

Geeta Kalia 1,90,000/-
 2127 of 2003 Anuraj Kalia 7,000/-
 2128 of 2003 Sarita Kalia 30,000/-
 2129 of 2003 Vikas Kalia 30,000/-
 2130 of 2003 Geeta Kalia 1,50,000/-
 Page N: 5 of 6  5 of 6 Anurag Kalia vs Satinder Singh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58309153/
5 FAO No. 2126 of 2003 & other connected cases 23.

The enhanced compensation shall be payable jointly and severally by respondents No.1 to 3, 3 along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the respective claim petitions till actual realization.
24. All the appeals are disposed of accordingly.
Copy of this order be placed on file of each appeal.
